{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Software License and Maintenance Agreement (Garman)

**To:** Deal team, Sparkling (Customer)
**From:** In-house counsel
**Re:** Playbook review of the Software License and Maintenance Agreement — verified findings and recommended positions

## Executive summary

We have completed our playbook review of the Garman Software License and Maintenance Agreement. The commercial architecture is workable and several areas are already at or better than our preferred position: there is no exclusivity or non-compete binding us, no minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitment, no most-favoured-nation obligation, no liquidated damages or early-termination fee, and no audit right running against us.

Three issues are critical and, in our view, must be resolved before signature. First, there is **no monetary cap on liability anywhere in the Agreement** (§ 15 excludes only indirect damages), leaving both parties — including us — with unlimited direct-damages exposure; we propose a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000 with a standard set of uncapped Excluded Claims. Second, **§ 13 gives Garman ownership of all IP in the Work "including any Improvements or Modifications thereto"**, which captures the bespoke Schedule "D" Modifications we commission and pay for, with no clear licence back and no confirmation that our data remains ours. Third, the **§ 13 indemnity is narrow**: it covers only breach of the title/non-infringement warranty, contains no duty to defend or settlement-control mechanic, omits breach of law, data incidents and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, does not extend to our affiliates, and conditions recovery on a strict ten-calendar-day notice.

At the high level, § 20(d) and § 3(c) impose a flat consent requirement on assignment with no affiliate, successor or reasonableness carve-out and no change-of-control provision — our stated walk-away position. The § 2 licence is likewise too narrow (affiliates only at Authorized Locations, no contractors, expressly non-transferable). Section 19 imposes a mutual outright **no-hire**, also a walk-away item, which we propose to convert to a narrow 12-month non-solicit. Remaining medium and low items include Nova Scotia governing law and venue (outside our accepted list), absent maintenance renewal mechanics and uplift cap, absent transition assistance and data return, a warranty with no stated remedy and no services/compliance/malicious-code warranties, a 90-day convenience termination notice with no refund of prepaid fees, and the absence of any vendor insurance covenant.

One finding — the AUDIT review (§ 1) — failed verification and should be re-run before we rely on it; the substantive conclusion recorded there is that no audit right binds us and no edit is required.

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue / position |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity | Indemnity limited to breach of title/non-infringement warranty; no duty to defend or settlement control, no coverage for breach of law, data incidents or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, no extension to affiliates, strict 10-day notice condition. Add defence/notice/cooperation procedure and standard additional heads; 3x annual fees super-cap available as fallback. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity | Garman owns all IP in the Work "including any Improvements or Modifications thereto", capturing customer-funded Schedule "D" Modifications, with no licence back (§ 2 covers only Software and Documentation) and no confirmation we retain rights in our data converted under § 4(b). Assign customer-funded Modifications to us with a licence back for embedded Garman IP, confirm our data remains ours, bar joint ownership. Fallback: Garman ownership plus perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 15 Limitation of Garman's Liability | No monetary cap anywhere in the Agreement; § 15 is only a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages, the heading is one-sided, and the sole carve-out is "breaches of Sections 13 and 14". Insert mutual cap at greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000 with uncapped Excluded Claims (confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), confirm fee obligations are not "damages", neutralise the heading. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | Page 10 (§ 20(d); see also § 3(c)) | Flat consent requirement with no affiliate or M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard (walk-away); § 3(c) additionally bars our assignment absent Garman's written authorisation; no change-of-control provision. Add affiliate/successor carve-out, reasonableness standard, competitor bar on Garman assignment, and confirm change of control is not an assignment and gives no termination or re-pricing right. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 Grant of License | Licence is perpetual while fees are paid, but covers affiliates only at Authorized Locations, omits contractors, and is expressly non-transferable with assignment barred (§ 3(c), § 20(d)), leaving no successor path. Extend to affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf (we remain responsible for compliance), delete "non-transferable" and permit transfer to a successor. |
| 6 | High | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees | Deviation | § 19 Non-Solicitation of Employees | Outright mutual no-hire ("not to hire or allow its respective affiliates to hire") covering any employee of the other party, with no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-outs and a period running from termination of the Agreement — a walk-away item. Taking the fallback: 12-month mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, with carve-outs, no-hire deleted. |
| 7 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 Grant of License | No exclusivity or sole-source obligation on us; "exclusive" references are licence scope, escrow, exclusive remedy and jurisdiction only. No redline. |
| 8 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 17 Term and Termination | No liquidated damages, penalties, late-payment interest or early-termination fee payable by us; § 17(b) convenience termination carries no fee, and termination amounts run in our favour under §§ 8(b) and 17(c). No redline. |
| 9 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 3 Restrictions on Use | § 3 restricts use of the licensed Work only (backup copies, no reverse engineering, no sublicence, no service bureau); § 19 is a non-solicit, not a non-compete. No field-of-use or territory covenant. No redline. |
| 10 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | Page 10 (§ 20 General Matters) | Nova Scotia law and Nova Scotia courts — counterparty's home jurisdiction, outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales); no arbitration provision elsewhere. Replace jurisdiction and forum wording only with New York law and exclusive jurisdiction of state and federal courts in New York County. |
| 11 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Missing | § 10 Maintenance and Support | § 10 refers to a "renewable one-year term" but there are no renewal mechanics, no non-renewal notice window, no vendor reminder and no cap on maintenance uplift, leaving renewal pricing undetermined. Add automatic 12-month renewals, 30-day customer opt-out, 60-day Garman renewal/price reminder, uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%; fallback 60-day/5%. |
| 12 | Medium | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | Missing | § 17 Term and Termination | § 17 addresses only our obligation to cease use and return/destroy Garman materials; no exit assistance and no obligation on Garman to return our data (including data converted under § 4(b)) or delete and certify deletion; § 18 survival is silent. Insert new § 17(d): six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of our data in machine-readable format within 30 days, then deletion with written certification. |
| 13 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 12 Specifications and Warranty | 12-month conformance warranty duration is acceptable and there is no implied-warranty disclaimer, but § 12 states no remedy; the only adjacent remedies are the time-limited § 7–8 rejection right ("in lieu of any other remedy") and "best efforts" Software Repair Service under § 10(c) conditional on paid maintenance. No services, compliance-with-laws or no-malicious-code warranty. Add a supplemental paragraph with a professional and workmanlike services standard, repair/replace/re-perform-or-refund remedy, compliance with laws and no malicious code, leaving the existing warranty intact. |
| 14 | Medium | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 17 Term and Termination | Direction is acceptable (we have a convenience right; Garman does not), but notice is 90 days rather than the preferred 30 and the clause is silent on refund of prepaid fees. Shorten to 30 days and add no-penalty pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; 60 days acceptable as fallback if the refund is retained. |
| 15 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation | Compliant | § 11 Fees | No MFN or best-pricing mechanic in either direction; §§ 10–11 simply require payment of Fee Schedule and maintenance fees. No redline. |
| 16 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 11 Fees | No minimum, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume obligation; § 2 charges extra fees only if we elect use beyond Authorized Locations; maintenance runs on a renewable one-year term with a 90-day exit under § 17(b). No redline. |
| 17 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 20 General Matters | Document-wide search returns no insurance covenant, yet Garman personnel attend Authorized Locations (§§ 4, 5) and convert our data. Insert new subsection (j): CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M for processing of our data, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request; fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M. |
| 18 | Low | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Needs review (verification failed) | § 1 Definitions and Schedules | Recorded conclusion is that no audit, inspection, records-examination or usage-verification right runs against us: § 14 is a mutual definitional confidentiality clause with no access mechanism, the Schedules contain no reporting or certification schedule, and § 17(b) is a one-off self-certification of destruction with no vendor access. Recommended action is no edit; however, this finding failed verification and should be re-run before we rely on it. |

## Walk-away items

Two findings engage express walk-away positions under our playbook:

1. **Assignment (Page 10, § 20(d), with § 3(c))** — a flat consent requirement on our assignment with no affiliate or M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard. We require an affiliate/successor carve-out, a reasonableness standard, and confirmation that a change of control of Sparkling is not an assignment and gives Garman no termination or re-pricing right.
2. **No-hire (§ 19)** — the outright mutual prohibition on hiring "any employee of the other party" is a walk-away item. Because the covenant is already mutual, we are prepared to take the fallback: a 12-month mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and the no-hire deleted.

We would also treat the absence of any liability cap (§ 15) as a must-fix: unlimited direct-damages exposure runs against us as well as Garman, and we should not sign without the mutual cap and Excluded Claims set.

## Next steps

1. Issue the redline reflecting the proposals above, leading with the three critical items (§ 15 mutual cap and Excluded Claims; § 13 ownership of customer-funded Modifications and our data; § 13 defence obligation and broadened indemnity heads with softened notice condition).
2. Table the two walk-away items (assignment/change of control; § 19 no-hire) as threshold conditions in the covering note, with the § 19 fallback offered up front.
3. Re-run the AUDIT check (§ 1) to clear the failed verification before we confirm to Garman that no change is required there.
4. Confirm with the business the acceptable fallbacks we are authorised to concede: 3x annual fees super-cap on indemnity; licence-back in lieu of assignment of Modifications; 60-day/5% renewal terms; 60 days' convenience notice with refund retained; E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M insurance limits.
5. On governing law, confirm that New York is our preferred landing and that no alternative from the accepted list (Delaware, California, England and Wales) is commercially preferable before we exchange drafts."}
